1	/*
     2	 * Model of the ticket system and correctness theorem
     3	 * Parts 4 and 5 in the paper
     4	 */
     5	type Process(==) = int  // Philosopher
     6	
     7	datatype CState = Thinking | Hungry | Eating  // Control states
     8	
     9	// A class can have state, with multiple fields, methods, a constructor, and declare functions and lemmas
    10	class TicketSystem
    11	{
    12	  var ticket: int  // Ticket dispenser
    13	  var serving: int  // Serving display
    14	
    15	  const P: set<Process>  // Fixed set of processes
    16	
    17	  // State for each process
    18	  var cs: map<Process, CState>  // (Partial) Map from process to state
    19	  var t: map<Process, int>  // (Partial) Map from process to ticket number
    20	
    21	  // Invariant of the system
    22	  // Checks that P is a subset of the domain/keys of each map
    23	  predicate Valid()
    24	    reads this  // Depends on the fields on the current class
    25	  {
    26	    && cs.Keys == t.Keys == P  // Alt. P <= cs.Keys && P <= t.Keys
    27	    && serving <= ticket
    28	    && (forall p ::  // ticket help is in range(serving, ticket)
    29	      p in P && cs[p] != Thinking
    30	      ==> serving <= t[p] < ticket
    31	    )
    32	    && (forall p, q ::  // No other process can have the ticket number equals to serving
    33	      p in P && q in P && p != q && cs[p] != Thinking && cs[q] != Thinking
    34	      ==> t[p] != t[q]
    35	    )
    36	    && (forall p ::  // We are serving the correct ticket number
    37	      p in P && cs[p] == Eating
    38	      ==> t[p] == serving
    39	    )
    40	  }
    41	
    42	  // Initialize the ticket system
    43	  constructor (processes: set<Process>)
    44	    ensures Valid()  // Postcondition
    45	    ensures P == processes  // Connection between processes and ts.P
    46	  {
    47	    P := processes;
    48	    ticket, serving := 0, 0;  // Alt. ticket := serving;
    49	    // The two following use map comprehension
    50	    cs := map p | p in processes :: Thinking;  // The map from p, where p in processes, takes value Thinking
    51	    t := map p | p in processes :: 0;
    52	  }
    53	
    54	  // The next three methods are our atomic events
    55	  // A Philosopher is Thinking and gets Hungry
    56	  method Request(p: Process)
    57	    requires Valid() && p in P && cs[p] == Thinking  // Control process precondition
    58	    modifies this  // Depends on the fields on the current class
    59	    ensures Valid()  // Postcondition
    60	  {
    61	    t, ticket := t[p := ticket], ticket + 1;  // Philosopher gets current ticket, next ticket's number increases
    62	    cs := cs[p := Hungry];  // Philosopher's state changes to Hungry
    63	  }
    64	
    65	  // A Philosopher is Hungry and enters the kitchen
    66	  method Enter(p: Process)
    67	    requires Valid() && p in P && cs[p] == Hungry  // Control process precondition
    68	    modifies this  // Depends on the fields on the current class
    69	    ensures Valid()  // Postcondition
    70	  {
    71	    if t[p] == serving  // The kitchen is available for this Philosopher
    72	    {
    73	      cs := cs[p := Eating];  // Philosopher's state changes to Eating
    74	    }
    75	  }
    76	
    77	  // A Philosopher is done Eating and leaves the kitchen
    78	  method Leave(p: Process)
    79	    requires Valid() && p in P && cs[p] == Eating  // Control process precondition
    80	    modifies this  // Depends on the fields on the current class
    81	    ensures Valid()  // Postcondition
    82	  {
    83	    //assert t[p] == serving;  // Ticket held by p is equal to serving
    84	    serving := serving + 1;  // Kitchen is ready to serve the next ticket holder
    85	    cs := cs[p := Thinking];  // Philosopher's state changes to Thinking
    86	  }
    87	
    88	  // Ensures that no two processes are in the same state
    89	  lemma MutualExclusion(p: Process, q: Process)
    90	    // Antecedents
    91	    requires Valid() && p in P
    92	    requires cs[p] == Eating && cs[q] == Eating
    93	    // Conclusion/Proof goal
    94	    ensures p == q
    95	  {
    96	
    97	  }
    98	}
    99	
   100	/*
   101	 * Event scheduler
   102	 * Part 6 in the paper
   103	 * Part 6.1 for alternatives
   104	 */
   105	method Run(processes: set<Process>)
   106	  requires processes != {}  // Cannot schedule no processes
   107	  decreases *  // Needed so that the loop omits termination checks
   108	{
   109	  var ts := new TicketSystem(processes);
   110	  var schedule := [];  // Scheduling choices
   111	  var trace := [(ts.ticket, ts.serving, ts.cs, ts.t)];  // Record sequence of states
   112	  
   113	  while true
   114	    invariant ts.Valid()
   115	    decreases *  // Omits termination checks
   116	  {
   117	    var p :| p in ts.P;  // p exists such that p is in ts.P
   118	    match ts.cs[p] {
   119	      case Thinking => ts.Request(p);
   120	      case Hungry => ts.Enter(p);
   121	      case Eating => ts.Leave(p);
   122	    }
   123	    schedule := schedule + [p];
   124	    trace:=trace + [(ts.ticket, ts.serving, ts.cs, ts.t)];
   125	  }
   126	}
   127	
   128	/*
   129	 * Event scheduler with planified schedule
   130	 * Part 6.2
   131	 */
   132	method RunFromSchedule(processes: set<Process>, schedule: nat -> Process)
   133	  requires processes != {}
   134	  requires forall n :: schedule(n) in processes
   135	  decreases *
   136	{
   137	  var ts := new TicketSystem(processes);
   138	  var n := 0;
   139	  
   140	  while true
   141	    invariant ts.Valid()
   142	    decreases *  // Omits termination checks
   143	  {
   144	    var p := schedule(n);
   145	    match ts.cs[p] {
   146	      case Thinking => ts.Request(p);
   147	      case Hungry => ts.Enter(p);
   148	      case Eating => ts.Leave(p);
   149	    }
   150	    n := n + 1;
   151	  }
   152	}
   153

content.text: Missing `q in P` in the lemma's precondition.

input.command:
cat > diagnosis.json <<'EOF'
{"spec_element": "requires",
 "proof_obligation": "bridge",
 "diagnosis": "MutualExclusion's precondition only states p in P, not q in P. So cs[q] is not well-formed (q may be outside cs's domain, error at line 92), and Valid()'s uniqueness facts only apply to processes in P, so p == q cannot be derived for an arbitrary q. Adding q in P to the requires clause fixes both."}
EOF
sed -i '91s/requires Valid() && p in P$/requires Valid() \&\& p in P \&\& q in P/' program.dfy && sed -n 91p program.dfy && dafny verify program.dfy

content.text:
Dafny now verifies `program.dfy` with 12 verified and 0 errors.

**Problem:** The `requires` clause of the `MutualExclusion` lemma said `p in P` but not `q in P`. That caused both errors:
- **Line 92:** `cs[q]` wasn't well-formed, because `q` might not be a key in `cs`.
- **Line 95:** `Valid()` only says that no two processes in `P` share a ticket while not thinking. With `q` possibly outside `P`, that fact couldn't be used, so `p == q` couldn't be proved.

**Fix:** I changed line 91 to `requires Valid() && p in P && q in P`. Nothing else in the file changed.

`diagnosis.json` records this as a `requires` / `bridge` issue.
